issues.legal_issue: A final decree in a partition suit may require a party to account when the preliminary decree, as modified on appeal, extends the accounting obligation to that party.
material_facts: The trial court’s preliminary decree required specified parties to render accounts.
On appeal, the preliminary decree was modified to require the named parties and the other parties to the suit to render accounts for their respective management of the properties.
The final decree imposed an accounting liability on a party who argued that the preliminary decree did not require that party to account.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary decree, as modified by the High Court, extended accounting to all parties to the suit, so the final decree’s accounting requirement was consistent with it.
issues.legal_principle: A final decree cannot amend or go behind a preliminary decree on a matter the preliminary decree has determined. The preliminary decree must, however, be read as modified on appeal; here, that modification extended the accounting obligation to the other parties to the suit. No earlier cases or specific statutory provisions were relied on for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_from_final_decree_in_partition_su: A party appealed from a final decree made in a partition suit.
predicates.preliminary_decree_modified_on_appeal: An appellate court modified the preliminary decree governing the suit.
predicates.modified_decree_extends_accounting_to_ot: The modified decree extended the duty to account to parties beyond those specifically required to account in the original decree.
predicates.final_decree_requires_party_to_account: The final decree required a party to account for that party’s management of the property.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a final decree in a partition suit follows a modified preliminary decree that extends accounting to other parties, a final decree may require a covered party to account.

issues.legal_issue: The costs of a partition suit may be borne by the estate.
material_facts: The proceeding was a partition suit.
The Court considered the nature of the suit when allocating the costs throughout the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The costs of the suit throughout were to be borne by the estate.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed that the costs throughout be borne by the estate because the proceeding was a partition suit; it cited no specific provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding was a suit seeking partition of an estate.

issues.definition: When the proceeding is a partition suit, the costs of the suit are borne by the estate.
